samples.summary: `packages/docs` knip workspace lists only `src/index.ts` as an entry (the `slides` workspace lists `src/node.ts` too), so the second public entry this delta extends is not treated as an entry point — nothing mechanically protects the Node-entry surface the frontend integration lane resolves.
samples.evidence: knip.json:14 `"entry": ["src/index.ts", "test/**/*.test.ts", "scripts/*.mjs"]` versus knip.json:30 for slides which includes `src/node.ts`. `packages/docs/package.json:14-33` exposes `./dist/node.js` (built from `src/node.ts`) under the `node` condition, and `packages/frontend/package.json:16` (`tsx --test tests/**/*.integration.ts`) resolves through it. Pre-existing config, but this delta is the second fix to that same drift.

finding.summary: `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` added to the browser entry (`src/index.ts`) but not to the Node entry (`src/node.ts`), which `YorkieDocStore` resolves to under the Node integration lane
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:38 imports `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` from '@wafflebase/docs'. packages/docs/package.json:14-26 gives that specifier a "node" condition resolving to ./dist/node.js, and packages/docs/src/node.ts:101-113 re-exports the block-helpers list WITHOUT `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` (only `applyMergeBlocks` at line 111). The comment at packages/docs/src/node.ts:95-100 states explicitly that `YorkieDocStore` imports these helpers from '@wafflebase/docs' and that the docs `.integration.ts` suite runs that store under Node, 'so the helpers must be re-exported here as well. Kept in sync with the browser entry (src/index.ts).' The store is loaded under Node by packages/frontend/tests/helpers/two-user-docs-yorkie.ts:2 (`import { YorkieDocStore } from '@/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts'`), used by packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store-concurrent.integration.ts:13, run via `tsx --test "tests/**/*.integration.ts"` (packages/frontend/package.json:16). An ESM named import that the module does not export fails at load time, so every Yorkie docs integration test file would fail to load, not just the merge case. No tsconfig path alias in packages/frontend/tsconfig.json redirects '@wafflebase/docs' to source. Fix belongs in packages/docs/src/node.ts: add `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` to the re-export block.

verdict.reason: The finding claims `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` is absent from the Node entry `packages/docs/src/node.ts`, causing an ESM named-import load failure for `YorkieDocStore`. It is present: `packages/docs/src/node.ts:112` re-exports `mergeDropsHeadingMemory` from `./store/block-helpers.js`, directly after `applyMergeBlocks` at :111, inside the exact export block (lines 101-114) the finding quotes as lacking it. The browser entry has the matching export at `packages/docs/src/index.ts:86`, so the two entries are in parity and the import at `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:38` resolves under either condition. A repo-wide grep for the symbol returns both entry files and the definition at `packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:279` — the reviewer's claim that this grep came up empty does not reproduce. There is also a parity test at `packages/docs/test/store/entry-parity.test.ts` that compares the re-export name sets of the two entries. One counterexample refutes this absence claim, and it is the specific line the fix was said to require.

finding.summary: Paste reaches the same 'heading memory travels onto text that was never a heading' defect the new merge guard closes, without passing through it
finding.evidence: The delta establishes the provenance rule that a `list-item`'s remembered `headingLevel` must not survive when foreign text is folded into the block (`mergeDropsHeadingMemory`, block-helpers.ts:279). The paste path bypasses it: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:3575-3580 appends the pasted inlines to the existing head block and then unconditionally sets `headBlock.type = firstPasted.type` and `headBlock.headingLevel = firstPasted.headingLevel`; the same happens for the tail block at lines 3604-3607. `copySelectedBlocks` copies the memory verbatim for a partial slice (text-editor.ts:3404: `if (block.headingLevel !== undefined) cloned.headingLevel = block.headingLevel;`), so pasting a bulleted heading into a paragraph makes the paragraph a `list-item` carrying a heading level, and the block's own pre-existing body text is then promoted to a Heading N on un-listing — exactly the #783 follow-up symptom. Confirming needs a paste round-trip test; the write path is unguarded either way. Fix could live either at these two assignments or by routing them through the same helper.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present exactly as described. block-helpers.ts:279-285 defines mergeDropsHeadingMemory and block-helpers.ts:293 applies it in applyMergeBlocks, establishing that a list-item's remembered headingLevel must not travel onto text that was never a heading. The paste path at text-editor.ts:3575-3581 and 3604-3610 appends foreign inlines into an existing block and then unconditionally assigns type/headingLevel from the pasted block, never consulting that helper; copySelectedBlocks (text-editor.ts:3404) preserves headingLevel even for a partial slice, so a bulleted-heading copy pasted into a paragraph yields a list-item carrying headingLevel over pre-existing body text. The consuming invariant is real: unlistedBlockType (model/types.ts:337-344) promotes any list-item with a defined headingLevel back to a heading, and memory.ts:249,260 deliberately keeps that memory across list conversion. No intervening normalization exists: updateBlockDirect (model/document.ts:432-435) forwards straight to store.updateBlock. This is a second, user-reachable write path bypassing a newly established invariant in another file — squarely the blast-radius lane, major impact.
